findings.where: Article page specimen, from the photograph to the PDF row (desktop-03/04, phone-03): the caption, the subhead 'So, what are the key chapter topics?', the bulleted list and the hairline above the lecture link
findings.fault: The vertical rhythm breaks right where content is added. The caption sits tight under the photograph. The subhead follows the caption with almost no gap, so the caption reads as belonging to the subhead rather than to the image above it (proximity). The list drops from the body's open leading to a cramped one, so on the phone each wrapped item runs into the next. The hairline touches the last line of the list, 'Cycle.'. The paragraphs above have generous spacing, so the article looks finely set until it reaches an image, a subhead or a list, and then looks broken.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who will add exactly these parts, and the founder, because the brief asked this specimen to prove the rhythm holds with an image, caption, list and subhead without hand-tuning. A development-bank reader reading Mark's article would also see the cramped list and the run-on caption as careless.

findings.where: First screen at phone width (phone-01): the portrait stacked above the heading, lead, tags and action
findings.fault: On the phone the portrait and its caption fill the whole first screen. Mark's line only starts below it, and the one action (the email box) comes after the lead and three rows of tag pills, about a screen and a half down. A phone visitor's first view is a passport-style headshot with no words of his and no way to reach him.
findings.who_objects: A development-agency officer opening a forwarded link on their phone. They have to scroll past the photo and a paragraph before they meet either the message or the contact. The brief asks for one message and one action on the first screen.

findings.where: First screen, the blue field behind the heading (desktop-01, phone-01): the ghost 'PPP' letters and the diagonal stripe pattern
findings.fault: Figure/ground: large pale 'PPP' letters sit straight behind the first two lines of the heading. Their bowls cross 'In my view, we are at' and 'a turning point', so the headline is read through a second, larger word. On the phone they are cropped at the right edge into a partial smudge. With the stripes over the whole field, the one calm field this direction is built on looks busy. It also contradicts the page's own texture note, which says 'one flat field, no grain'.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for one soft ground, restraint and nothing childish or techy; the doubled lettering reads as a decorative gimmick. A visitor would also find the heading slightly harder to take in at a glance.

findings.where: First screen, the row of five outlined tag pills (PPP Law, Infrastructure, Development banks, Governments, Risk allocation) between the lead and the action
findings.fault: The pills add a third band of boxed elements between the lead and the action. Similarity: they share the action's boxed, rectangular treatment, so the eye stops on five box-shaped things before reaching the one that acts. On the phone they wrap to three rows and push the action further down. The first screen then has a heading, a paragraph, a tag cloud and a button, where the brief asks for one message and one action.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor, who scans a row of what look like filters before finding how to write to Mark, and the founder, who judges this first screen against the one-message-one-action rule.

findings.where: Type pair section, the two columns (desktop-02/03): the 'In my view, Gelasio' specimen on the left and 'Source Sans 3' on the right
findings.fault: The two specimens neither share a top line nor a baseline. 'Source Sans 3' floats about 70 px lower than the Gelasio line, so its description starts at a different height from its neighbour's. The two-column pair reads as accidentally offset, not as a matched pair. In the palette row above, the texture column also leaves a tall empty block under its note, beside the long text-pair table.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the specimen parts, who would see a loose grid in the section meant to show the system's precision.

findings.where: Motion sketch frame at phone width (phone-03) compared with the phone hero (phone-01)
findings.fault: On the phone the sketch puts the portrait on the left and the heading on the right in a cramped two-column box. The real phone hero stacks the portrait above the heading. The sketch therefore shows a phone layout the page does not use, and its heading is squeezed into a narrow column of short lines.
findings.who_objects: The founder or a builder using the sketch to judge how the entrance looks on a phone; the sketch misrepresents the phone arrangement it is meant to preview.
